note: 'by making peace through the blood of His cross' (Col 1:20) -- the two figures in one phrase.

'the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God' (1Cor 1:18). **The instrument stands for the whole of it**, which is what lets Paul say he glories in it (Gal 6:14).

'a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing' (Rev 5:6), and 'Worthy is the Lamb, who was slain' (5:12). **Twenty-six of the twenty-eight Lamb verses are outside the gospels**, and most are here. Revelation never names him in these verses -- the Lamb is the name it uses -- so the pair rides on 5:5, where the Lion of Judah and the Root of David are named a verse before the Lamb appears.
'declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead' (Rom 1:4).; The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God
'you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power' (Mark 14:62), and 'because He is the Son of Man' (John 5:27).

'what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures' (1Cor 15:3). **Delivered what he received** -- Paul presents it as something handed to him rather than revealed to him, which is unusual for him.

'We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead ... we too may walk in newness of life' (Rom 6:4). The figure needs both halves and Romans gives both.
'Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?' (1Cor 15:55), and 'united with Him like this in His death' (Rom 6:5).
'in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.' (Rom 6:4). **The figure runs from him to the reader in one sentence.**
'since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.' (Rom 6:9).
'the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot' (1Pet 1:19), and 'He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood' (Heb 9:12).

'The blood on the houses where you are staying will be a sign; when I see the blood, I will pass over you.' (Exod 12:13). **The epistle's lamb without blemish is the passover requirement** (Exod 12:5), and 1 Peter uses the phrase without naming the feast.
'You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God' (Rev 5:9), and 'They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb' (12:11).
'the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin' (1John 1:7) beside 'God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf' (2Cor 5:21). Two writers, two figures, one exchange.
'God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,' (Gal 4:4), and 'God sent His one and only Son into the world' (1John 4:9).
'raised from the dead through the glory of the Father' (Rom 6:4). **The raising is attributed to the Father**, which is the ordinary form: he is more often raised than rising.
'God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.' (1John 5:11). **Seventeen of the Son verses are in 1 John's five chapters**, which is the densest use of it in the corpus.

'and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead' (Rom 1:4). **The resurrection is what declares it**, which is the letters' characteristic move: the title is argued for rather than announced.

The figure, back to the event. 'Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull ... There they crucified Him' (John 19:17–18). **Paul keeps the two words together**: 'the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me' (Gal 6:14) -- σταυρός and σταυρόω in one sentence; 'the message of the cross' (1Cor 1:18) is 'Christ crucified' (1:23).
